newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels advance toward town 240 miles from capital.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels advance toward town 240 miles from capital.

text.p: Zaire rebel leader Laurent Kabila said Friday his forces were advancing toward the town of Kikwit, 240 miles east of the capital Kinshasa.
He said his army was closing in on Kikwit after seizing Ilebo, Tshikapa and Dowete and they could arrive in the town in the next 48 hours.
Kabila, whose rebels have seized more than half of Zaire, said the battle for Kinshasa would come "sooner than expected and will be very, very swift."
"The force will be big and the firepower overwhelming and necessary to contain the notorious army" of President Mobutu Sese Seko, he said.
Kabila said he wanted face-to-face talks with Mobutu in South Africa or possibly Zambia and rejected all other proposed venues on security grounds.

"We need to meet the man (Mobutu) in a place where security is 100 percent guaranteed," he told Reuters, adding South Africa or perhaps Zambia were his only preferences for talks on the president's departure from power.
He did not mention Gabon as a venue for the talks, saying he was still prepared to meet Mobutu for talks on his "respectful departure from power" but the question was where.
Mobutu's son and spokesman said earlier the president would have no objection to meeting Kabila in Gabon for talks on ending Zaire's civil war.
"There's no official comment yet but it's no problem for the president," Nznaga Mobutu told Reuters when asked about his father's reaction to efforts to stage the talks in Gabon.

A regional military analyst who closely monitors the war between Kabila's rebels and the government army, said the rebels had stepped up their push on Kikwit, which was hit by an epidemic of the Ebola virus in 1995.
"We are very close to Kikwit and our forces should be there in the next 48 hours," Kabila said.
"After Kikwit, we will be very close to Kinshasa which is our final destination. We are moving fast and we are also consolidating an overwhelming force for the final battle of Kinshasa," he added.

A Zairian military official in Kinshasa said Wednesday it was possible the rebels had taken Ilebo and Tshikapa but was not sure about the capture of Dowete, a major town in Mobutu's home province of Equateur.

Ilebo is Zaire's largest inland port and second most important after its only Atlantic port at Matadi. It is the most vital link for goods destined for Kinshasa, transported by train from Lubumbashi and even South Africa, then transhipped by river to the capital.
